scheduler_rule.status: PROPOSED rule for the owner (A7 names the four states and the one-blocker rule; the derivation below is this lane's)
scheduler_rule.precedence: VERIFIED > RUNNING > BLOCKED > READY; the first condition that holds sets the state
scheduler_rule.VERIFIED: every governing document of the row's interface cell is owner-frozen (interface_status FROZEN) AND every S1a / S1 readiness condition the row references is SATISFIED in the committed readiness status files AND the row references at least one such condition
scheduler_rule.RUNNING: the row's single blocking item is worked by a REGISTERED H2 follow-on: the lane id is present in docs/orchestration/lane_registry_v1.json follow_ons (read, never pinned) and its registered scope (workflow script prompt, quoted verbatim and checked at build time) produces the missing input of that item
scheduler_rule.BLOCKED: a single named blocking item exists and no registered lane works it (an owner decision, an H-1 / C-1 measurement (A7 wave H4, PLANNED_NOT_REGISTERED), a procurement action (wave H3, PLANNED_NOT_REGISTERED) or an item outside every registered scope)
scheduler_rule.owner_decision_items: a blocking item whose resolved state is an open owner decision (state text matches 'owner decision' / OPEN_OWNER_DECISION) is never RUNNING: no lane can take an owner decision; enforced at build time
scheduler_rule.partial_scope: RUNNING needs registered scopes that produce EVERY missing input the blocking item names; when registered lanes cover only part of it (checked against the item's own 'requires' text), they are listed under partial_scope and the row stays BLOCKED
scheduler_rule.one_blocker_rule: every row carries exactly ONE blocking evidence/interface item (typed id resolved against its defining file); A7: every BLOCKED row points to exactly one item
scheduler_rule.lanes_that_mature_but_do_not_work_the_bl: an H2 lane that matures other aspects of a row is listed under h2_lanes but does not change the execution state
scheduler_rule.live_execution_state_of_lanes: not read: the trigger ledgers are mutable and time-varying; RUNNING means 'assigned by registration and scope', not 'an agent is executing now'

rule.status: PROPOSED rule for the owner (A7 names the four states and the one-blocker rule; the derivation below is this lane's)
rule.precedence: VERIFIED > RUNNING > BLOCKED > READY; the first condition that holds sets the state
rule.VERIFIED: every governing document of the row's interface cell is owner-frozen (interface_status FROZEN) AND every S1a / S1 readiness condition the row references is SATISFIED in the committed readiness status files AND the row references at least one such condition
rule.RUNNING: the row's single blocking item is worked by a REGISTERED H2 follow-on: the lane id is present in docs/orchestration/lane_registry_v1.json follow_ons (read, never pinned) and its registered scope (workflow script prompt, quoted verbatim and checked at build time) produces the missing input of that item

rule.partial_scope: RUNNING needs registered scopes that produce EVERY missing input the blocking item names; when registered lanes cover only part of it (checked against the item's own 'requires' text), they are listed under partial_scope and the row stays BLOCKED
rule.one_blocker_rule: every row carries exactly ONE blocking evidence/interface item (typed id resolved against its defining file); A7: every BLOCKED row points to exactly one item
rule.lanes_that_mature_but_do_not_work_the_bl: an H2 lane that matures other aspects of a row is listed under h2_lanes but does not change the execution state
rule.live_execution_state_of_lanes: not read: the trigger ledgers are mutable and time-varying; RUNNING means 'assigned by registration and scope', not 'an agent is executing now'
